title: Token-efficiency evaluator
description: Thresholds and refusal conditions for the paired token-efficiency benchmark (#225). The version is carried by every verdict, so a published result names the rules that judged it.

version.description: Bumped in the same commit as any change below. Travels with every verdict.

thresholds.description: Kept as separate thresholds rather than folded into a score: folding lets a large win on one buy a loss on another.

maxMedianInputRatio.description: Median compiled input context as a fraction of baseline. Must be above zero: a threshold of zero would accept only a compiled arm that read nothing, which is not a benchmark.

maxMedianSessionRatio.description: Median full-session tokens as a fraction of baseline. Not capped at 1 in the schema, because a policy may deliberately allow a session regression while a separate threshold holds the input claim -- but the shipped value is 1.00.

maxMeanQualityDrop.description: Applies ONLY to runs that already passed the required-evidence count. A mean never compensates for a missing evidence item.

refuseWhen.description: Conditions under which no verdict is produced at all. Each is a refusal rather than a failing score, because a failing score is a measurement and these are the cases where no measurement exists.

anyCostUnavailable.description: Not configurable. A cost the runtime cannot observe is not zero, and a harness permitted to treat it as zero would reward moving work out of view.

armsAsymmetric.description: Not configurable. Two arms given different inputs are not a comparison.

corpusDigestMismatch.description: Not configurable. A corpus edited after the freeze makes every number correct arithmetic about a corpus nobody agreed to.

anyRequiredEvidenceMissing.description: Not configurable, and const rather than boolean on purpose: this is the one threshold whose relaxation produces an arithmetically CORRECT number about the wrong population.

oracleReachableFromAnArm.description: Not configurable. An arm that can read its own answers measures nothing.
